candidates.source_title: Five Lamborghinis and Mercedes seized after motorway driving reports - Roch Valley Radio
candidates.source_body_excerpt:
Greater Manchester Police said the vehicles were being driven at high speeds, weaving between lanes, wheel spinning and at times slowing to around 17mph on the motorway.

Officers from GMP's Transport Policing and Crime Command responded to the reports on Wednesday evening, September 2.

The force's Roads Policing Unit was told a group of high-powered vehicles were being driven on the M66.

Police later found the convoy on the M62 and stopped two Lamborghinis as they left the motorway.

Specialist tactics were then used to stop the remaining vehicles in Rochdale.

Five Lamborghinis and a Mercedes G-Wagon were seized under Section 59 of the Police Reform Act 2002.

GMP said the drivers were prosecuted for a number of driving offences.

Chief Inspector Danny Kabal, from GMP's Transport Policing and Crime Command, said: “We take road safety very serious in GMP, and we will not tolerate careless, inconsiderate, anti-social or dangerous driving on our roads.

“People who think it is acceptable to use our roads as a racetrack, need to pay attention to this result and take it as a warning – they will have their vehicles seized and they will be prosecuted. Where proportionate to do so, they will also be arrested.”

Police temporarily closed the road while dealing with the vehicles.

Chief Inspector Kabal thanked members of the public who reported the driving and asked anyone with footage of the incident, including dashcam or CCTV recordings, to contact GMP.

Information can be provided by calling 101 or through www.gmp.police.uk. Road traffic footage can also be submitted through GMP's Operation Snap service.
candidates.source_summary: Five Lamborghinis and a Mercedes G-Wagon have been seized after police received reports of dangerous driving on the M66 and M62.

candidates.source_title: Victims of addiction: Hospital admissions, early deaths and teens in treatment - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: More than 170 teenagers received treatment for alcohol and drug abuse with demand for the borough’s addiction services rising among young people and adults. As the numbers receiving treatment reach the highest levels since Covid — including long-term drinking causing increasing harm to adults — Rochdale Council’s Health, Schools and Care Overview and Scrutiny Committee meets on Wednesday when it will hear about the steps being taken to tackle tobacco, vaping, drugs, alcohol and gambling addiction. In a report to the committee, Kuiama Thompson, Director of Public Health and Communities, said: “Drug and alcohol harm continues to have a significant impact on the health of Rochdale borough residents, contributing to avoidable hospital admissions, premature mortality, pressure on health and care services, and widening health inequalities. “It also has a wider impact on society and the economy, such as contributing to safeguarding concerns, crime, homelessness and unemployment.” Figures from the National Drug Treatment Monitoring System estimate that there are 1,831 people who use opiates and crack cocaine in the borough and 2,905 who have an alcohol dependency. Teenagers have been receiving treatment for cannabis addiction Ms Thompson added: “There is no evidence that more people in the Rochdale borough are drinking alcohol overall, but the harm caused is increasing. This may be due to the health impact of long-term heavy drinking reflecting drinking patterns from a decade or more ago with deprivation being a major driver. This highlights the ongoing and disproportionate burden of alcohol-related harm within the borough. “The main substances causing young people to access treatment with Early Break are cannabis and alcohol. Strong pathways have been established to identify if young people are presenting to health services with bladder, mental health or school issues without disclosing ketamine or other drug use.

candidates.source_title: Town of Culture year brings in at least £5.5m for Rochdale - Roch Valley Radio
candidates.source_body_excerpt:
Rochdale’s year as Greater Manchester’s Town of Culture raked in more than £5.5m for the local economy, according to council data.

A report looking into the value for money of the Town of Culture status found that the Rochdale borough attracted 213,099 attendees over 297 events throughout the 2025/2026 year. Rochdale council’s evaluation has reported more than £5.5m in leisure, based on a low estimated spend of £25 per head. 

An assessment carried out by Marketing Manchester suggested a daily visitor spend of £78, meaning there was potential that the boost to the local economy could actually be as high as £16.6m.

Given the council secured £50,000 from the GMCA Culture Fund to support cultural activities between April 2025 and March 2026, council papers suggest Greater Manchester’s Town of Culture was good value for money.

The local authority teamed up with Rochdale Development Agency (RDA) and other partners to deliver a huge number of cultural events across the borough. Animals being brought to life in ‘The Herds’, Street Eat, Rochdale Comedy Festival, Rochdale Pride and Ignite Fire Festival are just some of the major highlights delivered for locals throughout the year. 

Hundreds of thousands of pounds in advertising and investments for external bodies, huge increase in footfall and paid opportunities for artists, freelancers and creative workers are other benefits listed in a town hall report.

The local authority isn’t resting on its laurels either. They are continuing to put on big events for the borough and intend to do so long into the future.

Councillor Sue Smith, cabinet member for communities and co-operation, said: “Rochdale’s year as Greater Manchester Town of Culture was a huge success, attracting more than 213,000 people to enjoy nearly 300 events, generating well over £5.5m for our local economy. Just as importantly, it showcased the very best of our borough and created positive publicity that reflected so well on Rochdale. 

“It is particularly encouraging that 94 per cent of attendees felt the events enhanced Rochdale’s image. We also saw a significant increase in engagement with younger audiences and a wide range of diverse communities. 

“This demonstrates how culture can bring people together, widen access, increase representation and encourages greater participation among residents. I am incredibly proud of what was achieved in just one year, and grateful to everyone who played a part in making it such a success. 

“The momentum created provides a strong platform for future cultural investment and events, and we are building on that legacy in the months and years ahead.”
candidates.source_summary: Rochdale’s year as Greater Manchester’s Town of Culture raked in more than £5.5m for the local economy, according to council data.

candidates.source_title: Veterans to run new café in restored Rochdale manor house - Roch Valley Radio
candidates.source_body_excerpt:
The ground floor of Denehurst House in Denehurst Park will be run by a local organisation supporting former armed forces personnel.

The café will be managed by Community Interest Company Get Together After Serving, known as GTAS, and staffed by veterans and members of their families.

GTAS was set up by Rochdale residents Adam Trennery, Wayne Traynor and Wayne Simms and provides support for veterans through wellbeing programmes, events and get-togethers.

The café will serve hot and cold sandwiches, cakes, breakfasts, tea and coffee. The organisation also plans to work with other local businesses to offer Friday specials.

Rochdale Borough Council owns Denehurst House and commissioned local builders H Bell and Sons and interior design specialists to renovate the building.

Period features including its ornate coving and bay windows have been retained.

The council is considering using the remainder of Denehurst House as accommodation for local veterans and has completed a public consultation on the proposal.

Councillor Danny Meredith, cabinet member for housing and regeneration, said: “This has been a really important project for us and it’s great to see it coming to fruition.

“Not only was this a derelict old building, which has been lovingly brought back to life, but it will be run by local veterans and their loved ones.”

Adam Trennery, a director of GTAS and local veteran, said: “We’re made up to have the opportunity to open a café in this brilliant space. It means a lot to me personally, as I live round the corner and I’ve always thought having a café in that lovely park would be great.

“We’re really excited that we can use this as a base to further our support for veterans, while also welcoming the wider community.”

Denehurst House was built for Alderman Robert Turner, founder of Turner Brothers Asbestos company, in the 1890s.

The house and its grounds were donated to the town in 1932 and the building was later used as council offices before becoming empty.

The café formally opens on Saturday, September 5.

It will open every day from 9am until 6pm between May and October and from 9am until 4pm between November and April.
candidates.source_summary: A 19th century manor house in Rochdale which has stood empty for years has been restored, with a new café opening on Saturday.

candidates.source_title: Don’t lose your vote - residents reminded to check voter registration details – Rochdale Borough Council
candidates.source_body_excerpt: The borough's residents are being urged to check their electoral registration details or risk losing their chance to vote on decisions that affect them. With local elections taking place in May 2027, it's an opportunity for residents to make sure they can take part. The annual canvass allows Rochdale Borough Council to keep the electoral register up to date, to identify who risks losing their voice at elections, and encourage them to register before it’s too late. Edward McCreadie, elections manager at Rochdale Borough Council, said: “Over the summer we've sent emails to residents in over 40,000 properties asking them to check their details and update if necessary and this week follow up letters were sent, so do keep an eye out. The annual canvass is our way of making sure that the information on the electoral register for every address is accurate and up to date. To make sure you don’t lose your say at upcoming elections, simply follow the instructions sent to you. If you’re not currently registered, your name will not appear in the messages we send. If you want to register, the easiest way is at rochdale.gov.uk/RegisterToVote." Local elections will be taking place in May 2027. Recent home movers, in particular, are urged to check their details. Electoral Commission research has found that recent home movers are less likely to be registered than those who have lived at the same address for a long time. In Great Britain, 92% of those who have lived in their home for 16 years will be registered, compared with 36% of people who have lived at an address for less than a year. Residents aged 16 and above can be added to the electoral register, but they can't vote until they are 18.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale’s year as Greater Manchester’s Town of Culture raked in more than £5.5m for the local economy, according to council data. A report looking into the value for money of the Town of Culture status found that the Rochdale borough attracted 213,099 attendees over 297 events throughout the 2025/2026 year. Rochdale council ’s evaluation has reported more than £5.5m in leisure, based on a low estimated spend of £25 per head. An assessment carried out by Marketing Manchester suggested a daily visitor spend of £78, meaning there was potential that the boost to the local economy could actually be as high as £16.6m. Click here to get the biggest stories straight to your inbox in our Daily Newsletter Given the council secured £50,000 from the GMCA Culture Fund to support cultural activities between April 2025 and March 2026, council papers suggest Greater Manchester’s Town of Culture was good value for money. The local authority teamed up with Rochdale Development Agency (RDA) and other partners to deliver a huge number of cultural events across the borough. Animals being brought to life in ‘The Herds’, Street Eat, Rochdale Comedy Festival, Rochdale Pride and Ignite Fire Festival are just some of the major highlights delivered for locals throughout the year. Hundreds of thousands of pounds in advertising and investments for external bodies, huge increase in footfall and paid opportunities for artists, freelancers and creative workers are other benefits listed in a town hall report. The local authority isn’t resting on its laurels either. They are continuing to put on big events for the borough and intend to do so long into the future. Councillor Sue Smith, cabinet member for communities and co-operation, said: “Rochdale’s year as Greater Manchester Town of Culture was a huge success, attracting more than 213,000 people to enjoy nearly 300 events, generating well over £5.5m for our local economy. Just as importantly, it showcased the very best of our borough and created positive publicity that reflected so well on Rochdale. “It is particularly encouraging that 94 per cent of attendees felt the events enhanced Rochdale’s image. We also saw a significant increase in engagement with younger audiences and a wide range of diverse communities. “This demonstrates how culture can bring people together, widen access, increase representation and encourages greater participation among residents. I am incredibly proud of what was achieved in just one year, and grateful to everyone who played a part in making it such a success. “The momentum created provides a strong platform for future cultural investment and events, and we are building on that legacy in the months and years ahead.”

candidates.source_title: Big problem remains: The big talking points from Shrewsbury Town’s Rochdale defeat - shropshirestar.com
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Losing football matches will happen. It was always going to happen for Shrewsbury Town. But this was a second very poor showing in the space of seven days. Managers sometimes talk about there being a ‘way to lose a game’. This was not it. Just like at Fleetwood Town seven days earlier, Salop were dismantled and there was never really a feeling they were going to find a way back into the game. Here are some talking points from Town’s miserable night at Rochdale. Boss Gavin Cowan stuck with his winning side, making just one change to the bench as Kian McMahon-Brown came in. But Town could not replicate the performance that had earned victory over Salford City. As Cowan admitted afterwards, several individuals were simply missing on the night and well below the level required. Town had been resilient and resolute to claim a first clean sheet of the season against Salford. That defensive solidity disappeared again at Rochdale. Salop have now conceded 12 goals in their opening five games, while scoring just three. And that brings us back to the biggest problem they struggled with last season: goals. So far, the summer recruits have done little to suggest that issue has been solved. The midfield was passive as Luca Hoole was isolated and beaten for the cross that led to Rochdale’s opener, while Josh Ruffels’ mis-clearance presented the hosts with their second. Sound familiar? It was only seven days earlier that Town had been punished for similar mistakes at Fleetwood. For the final blow, Town were dispossessed far too easily and Rochdale broke quickly, with Will Brook staying rooted to the edge of his six-yard box as the goal gaped. Captain Will Boyle had been Town’s hero against Salford. He can take some credit for his efforts again, but there was little he could do to rescue his side this time around - making it a disappointing night for the birthday boy. Shrewsbury have now failed to score in each of their last four away league games. They last endured a longer run without scoring on the road in November 2023 - when they also went four games without finding the net. Town altered their shape several times throughout the game. They started with a back four rather than the back five used previously and moved into a 4-4-1-1 towards the end of the first half. They appeared to switch again to a 4-2-3-1 after the break as Cowan looked for a way back into the game. Kian McMahon-Brown made his Town debut just a day after joining on a season-long loan from Burnley. He replaced Isaac Fletcher, who struggled to make a significant impact. Town will hope McMahon-Brown can provide some of the spark going forward that has been missing, with supporters hoping he can have a similar impact to Iwan Morgan’s loan spell last season. There was also a first glimpse of Michael Golding, who replaced Tom Sang. The Leicester City loanee went close late on, with his low effort being blocked. Just as they did after the defeat at Fleetwood, Town have now set themselves the task of responding to another miserable night. They have little time to dwell on it, with a trip to Fleetwood next up and a chance to produce a very different outcome to their EFL Cup thrashing there.

candidates.source_title: Ian Watson lauds Rochdale’s ‘courage and bravery’ in win over Shrewsbury - largsandmillportnews.com
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale produced the kind of performance boss Ian Watson has been waiting for as they swept Shrewsbury aside with a 3-0 victory at the Crown Oil Arena. Baba Adeeko fired them ahead in the 33rd minute before Luke Hannant lofted a beautiful finish over Shrews stopper Will Brook 10 minutes later. Dale goalkeeper Nils Ramming pulled off a fine save after the break to keep out Will Boyle’s header, but the home side’s lead was never under threat and they rounded off a fine display with substitute Jonny Smith firing into the roof of the net in the 80th minute. It was the club’s first win since returning to the EFL and the first three-point return of Watson’s tenure. He said: “I never get obsessed with the scoreboard, it’s been performances that have not looked as we wanted them to look, so it was the way we played, the courage and bravery we showed, that was the most pleasing thing. “We needed to get that first win over the line. We’d spoken about not being anxious and not playing the scoreboard but playing how we want to play and enjoying being out there. “You could see we were playing without fear. The boys want to win so much and run so hard that it can sometimes manifest as anxiety. We’ve been playing with a little bit of fear, being shy with the ball. “That’s been the hard thing for me as a coach, you want it to look a certain way and it hasn’t been that – tonight it was that. Now we have to make sure that is us every week.”

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale produced the kind of performance boss Ian Watson has been waiting for as they swept Shrewsbury aside with a 3-0 victory at the Crown Oil Arena. Baba Adeeko fired them ahead in the 33rd minute before Luke Hannant lofted a beautiful finish over Shrews stopper Will Brook 10 minutes later. Dale goalkeeper Nils Ramming pulled off a fine save after the break to keep out Will Boyle’s header, but the home side’s lead was never under threat and they rounded off a fine display with substitute Jonny Smith firing into the roof of the net in the 80th minute. It was the club’s first win since returning to the EFL and the first three-point return of Watson’s tenure. He said: “I never get obsessed with the scoreboard, it’s been performances that have not looked as we wanted them to look, so it was the way we played, the courage and bravery we showed, that was the most pleasing thing. “We needed to get that first win over the line. We’d spoken about not being anxious and not playing the scoreboard but playing how we want to play and enjoying being out there. “You could see we were playing without fear. The boys want to win so much and run so hard that it can sometimes manifest as anxiety. We’ve been playing with a little bit of fear, being shy with the ball. “That’s been the hard thing for me as a coach, you want it to look a certain way and it hasn’t been that – tonight it was that. Now we have to make sure that is us every week.”

candidates.source_title: Gavin Cowan slams Shrewsbury Town players after Rochdale defeat - shropshirestar.com
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A deflated Gavin Cowan said his Shrewsbury Town side were “devoid of any desire to win” in a miserable night at Rochdale. The Salop boss delivered a lengthy response to his first question after Town’s 3-0 defeat in Greater Manchester, laying into his players after another poor display. Shrewsbury failed to build on their first League Two win days earlier, suffering a third defeat in four league matches, and without scoring. “Disappointment is an understatement,” said boss Cowan. “First of all, it’s such a long way to come for the fans. I am gutted that we couldn’t put on more of a show. “Gutted that they’ve had to travel on a Tuesday night for us to not perform. “We’ve had 16 shots and it didn’t even feel like we were going to score. “I thought we were really poor. What’s hard for me is I don’t know what I’m going to get from my players. And that’s on me, obviously I’ve signed them. “I’ve always said that their ability is on me. Their conditioning is obviously a combination of them and us. Mentality is them - and tonight for me was all about mentality. “They were devoid of any desire to win. I think we were missing six or seven lads who were just really poor. “Sometimes in these games, you carry a couple, the lads rally round, get round them. But tonight, I am really disappointed. “It hurts. Getting a little boo from the fans, I understand it. I’m gutted, it absolutely hurts.” Town found themselves two goals down at the break after being punished for mistakes and poor defending, before Rochdale added a third 10 minutes from time. Cowan said his side also “lacked bravery” and gave the ball away too easily in another disappointing night on the road - just a week after they were thrashed 4-0 by Fleetwood Town in the EFL Cup. “There’s some unbelievable players in our changing room, there’s an array of talent,” Cowan added. “It’s really balanced in terms of how we want to play. But our minimum requirements are hard work, desire, and do a job-and-a-half. “Too many of them didn’t do that. Too many of them didn’t do that tonight. So apologies to everyone.”

candidates.source_title: Rochdale register maiden league win after easing past Shrewsbury - prestwichandwhitefieldguide.co.uk
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale picked up their first win since returning to the EFL with a 3-0 victory against Shrewsbury at the Crown Oil Arena. Ian Watson’s men registered their threat 20 minutes in when Kane Taylor crossed for Dajaune Brown, whose header skimmed the crossbar. They deservedly took the lead in the 33rd minute. Emmanuel Dieseruvwe’s shot was blocked and Brown, with his back to goal, fed the rebound to Baba Adeeko, who stroked a right-footed effort beyond goalkeeper Will Brook. The home side underlined their increasing dominance with a second on 43 minutes. Luke Hannant seized on a slip by Josh Ruffels to collect Dieseruvwe’s pass and race through unchallenged, lifting a sumptuous finish over Brook from 18 yards. After the break, Joe Gbode fired across the face of goal from a tight angle before Nils Ramming pulled off a fine save to keep out Will Boyle’s header. Substitute Jonny Smith rounded off the scoring in the 80th minute, racing through on the right and curling a decisive shot beyond Brook.

candidates.source_title: Care provider’s plans to raise the roof - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A care provider’s bid to replace the roof and change the appearance of its offices and distribution centre in Middleton have been refused because they are “out of character” with the surrounding area. Vestacare provides support for adults with learning disabilities through day and supported-living services. The company applied to Rochdale Council for planning permission to replace the existing asbestos roof and external cladding and extend the shallow pitched roof over the whole building at Unit 1 Westcroft Industrial Estate, 582 Manchester Old Road. In a design and access statement submitted with the application, the company said: “The proposal seeks consent for the refurbishment and rationalisation of the existing industrial building including the removal of aging asbestos cement roof sheeting and external cladding materials, together with the installation of a new insulated roof and external wall cladding system. “The existing roof forms are fragmented and visually inconsistent. The surrounding industrial estate contains a range of commercial and industrial buildings of varying ages and appearances. “A number of adjacent units within the estate have already undergone refurbishment works involving replacement cladding and modern metal roof systems. The proposal therefore reflects the ongoing regeneration and modernisation of the wider industrial estate environment. “The improved roof structure and increased internal clearance heights will facilitate a more efficient internal storage and distribution arrangement for Vestacare’s wider care home operations. “The building functions as a central operational support and distribution facility serving a number of care homes within the wider region.

While it was in force it provided officers with enhanced stop-and-search powers, enabling them to order youths to remove all face coverings and leave the defined area covered. She did speak about the expansion of the tram network to Stockport in her manifesto, but Heywood was omitted. It falls under what TfGM calls the Oldham-Rochdale-Heywood-Bury Tram-Train pathfinder. candidates.source_title: Modern house overlooking lake ‘won’t harm Green Belt’, inspector rules - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Plans to create a modern five-bedroom home overlooking Hollingworth Lake can go ahead after an appeal ruled it does not affect the openness of the Green Belt. Rochdale Council refused planning permission for the demolition of the current two-storey, four-bedroom house at Hollingworth Heights, Peanock Lane, Littleborough, replacing it with a larger, modern property. The plans include increasing the existing floor area of 342m2 to 546m2 and an increase in volume of approximately 80%. In refusing the application, the council said: “The proposed development comprises inappropriate development in the Green Belt that is harmful by definition and furthermore, fails to preserve the openness of the Green Belt. “Additionally, the proposed development would have an unacceptable impact on the character and appearance of the application site and the surrounding area including the special qualities and characteristics of the landscape setting.” Applicant Olivia McKee appealed against the refusal and the Planning Inspectorate has upheld that appeal, granting planning permission for the development to go ahead. In reaching her decision, planning inspector Elaine Moulton said in her report: “While the increase in volume would be significant, openness is not determined solely by volumetric comparisons. “The proposal would increase the building footprint by 11%, which, in the context of the overall site, would be modest.
